title: JWST/NIRSpec Reveals Diverse Nuclear Environments in Dwarf Galaxies Hosting AGN
comment: 27 pages, 12 figures, 4 tables. Accepted to ApJ
summary: Dwarf galaxies, in the $Λ$CDM framework, are expected to dominate the galaxy number density at all redshifts. As such, studying AGN in these systems, including characterizing their local environments and emission properties, is essential in obtaining a comprehensive view of the AGN population and their influence on their host galaxy. To this end, we present JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of four dwarf galaxies (M$_\star<$10$^{9.5}\;$M$_\odot$) with evidence of AGN activity. Utilizing the improvements in resolution and sensitivity offered by JWST, we investigate the emission features of the central kiloparsec of these dwarfs. Our findings include the detection of over 100 emission lines across our sample, including coronal lines with ionization potentials greater than 300 eV. The nuclear spectra show diverse emission features. In two galaxies, we measure strong contributions from hot dust to the infrared continuum. We also detect both PAH and coronal line emission within 100 parsecs of the nuclei in three galaxies. We estimate the hot H$_2$ gas mass to be between 1--20 M$_\odot$ within 300 pc across our sample, where both thermal and non-thermal excitation are involved. Lastly, spatial flux maps reveal varied emission structures across all observed gas phases, ranging from radial symmetry around the nucleus to elongated plumes. Kinematic maps also show each galaxy has unique velocity structures despite all being isolated, affirming the diversity of rotation curves problem, a long standing tension between simulations and observations. These results showcase the unique and varied nuclear environments that can be found in dwarf galaxies hosting AGN.

AI.tldr: This paper presents JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of four dwarf galaxies with evidence of AGN activity. The authors detect over 100 emission lines, including coronal lines with ionization potentials exceeding 300 eV, measure hot dust contributions in two galaxies, detect PAH and coronal line emission within 100 pc of the nuclei in three galaxies, estimate hot H2 gas masses of 1-20 M_sun within 300 pc, and reveal diverse emission and kinematic structures that affirm the diversity of rotation curves problem in dwarf galaxies.
AI.motivation: Dwarf galaxies are expected to dominate galaxy number density in the ΛCDM framework at all redshifts, yet AGN in these low-mass systems remain poorly understood. Characterizing their local environments and emission properties is essential for obtaining a comprehensive understanding of the AGN population and AGN-host galaxy feedback, particularly given the low-mass regime offers critical tests of galaxy formation models.
AI.method: The authors use JWST/NIRSpec Integral Field Unit (IFU) observations of four dwarf galaxies (M_star < 10^9.5 M_sun) with evidence of AGN activity. They exploit JWST's improved resolution and sensitivity to investigate emission features in the central kiloparsec, producing nuclear spectra, spatial flux maps of all gas phases, and kinematic maps across the sample.
AI.result: Over 100 emission lines detected across the sample, including coronal lines with ionization potentials >300 eV. Two galaxies show strong hot dust contributions to the infrared continuum. PAH and coronal line emission detected within 100 pc of nuclei in three galaxies. Hot H2 gas masses estimated between 1-20 M_sun within 300 pc, with both thermal and non-thermal excitation. Spatial maps reveal varied emission structures from radial symmetry to elongated plumes, and kinematic maps show unique velocity structures despite all galaxies being isolated.
AI.conclusion: These results showcase the unique and varied nuclear environments found in dwarf galaxies hosting AGN, and the kinematic diversity observed affirms the long-standing "diversity of rotation curves" problem—a tension between ΛCDM simulations and observations that persists even in isolated dwarf systems.

title: Super-Eddington Accretion and Early-Stage Feedback in Ton S180
comment: 15 pages (main text), 8 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A (1 September 2026)
summary: Narrow-line Seyfert 1 (NLSy1) galaxies are key laboratories for studying rapid supermassive black hole (SMBH) growth and active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback at high accretion rates. We investigate the nearby NLSy1 Ton S180 with VLT-MUSE optical integral field spectroscopy to connect its nuclear accretion properties with the spatially resolved ionized gas and host-galaxy kinematics. We modeled the unresolved nuclear spectrum and applied a custom point spread function subtraction to recover the host-galaxy emission on kiloparsec scales. The nuclear spectrum requires a complex permitted-line decomposition and a blueshifted [O III] outflow component. Single-epoch estimators and the stellar velocity dispersion imply black hole masses in the range $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot) = 6.5 - 7.7$. Combined with the observed luminosity, this implies a dimensionless mass accretion rate of $\dot{M} / \dot{M}_{\rm Edd} = 4.1 - 980$, confirming the extreme accretion regime. The host galaxy shows a circumnuclear ring, an inner elongated structure consistent with a bar, and rotation-dominated gas and stellar kinematics. Simple inflow models do not significantly better reproduce the observed velocity field. We detect a resolved ionized outflow extending about 2 kpc west of the nucleus, with mildly blueshifted velocities (with a maximum of $v_{\rm max} \sim 340$ km s$^{-1}$). Its mass outflow rate is only $\sim 4.2 \times 10^{-4}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, whereas the unresolved nuclear outflow reaches $v_{\rm max} \sim 1140$ km s$^{-1}$ and $\dot{M}_{\rm out} > 1.5\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. This contrast may reflect either weak ionized coupling from nuclear to galactic scales or different episodes of AGN activity over time. These results show that Ton S180 is undergoing rapid SMBH growth, while the observed ionized outflow remains confined to the inner few kiloparsecs and is weak on host-galaxy scales.

AI.tldr: The paper presents VLT-MUSE optical integral field spectroscopy of the nearby Narrow-line Seyfert 1 galaxy Ton S180. The authors decompose the nuclear spectrum, subtract the PSF, and recover host-galaxy emission on kiloparsec scales. Black hole mass estimates (log M_BH/M_sun = 6.5–7.7) imply an extreme accretion regime (Mdot/Mdot_Edd = 4.1–980). The host shows a circumnuclear ring, a bar-like structure, and rotation-dominated kinematics. A resolved ionized outflow extends ~2 kpc west with low mass outflow rate (~4.2×10^-4 M_sun/yr), contrasting with the unresolved nuclear outflow (v~1140 km/s, Mdot>1.5 M_sun/yr), suggesting weak ionized coupling between scales or episodic AGN activity.
AI.motivation: NLSy1 galaxies are key laboratories for studying rapid supermassive black hole (SMBH) growth and AGN feedback at high accretion rates. The authors aim to connect the nuclear accretion properties of Ton S180 with its spatially resolved ionized gas and host-galaxy kinematics.
AI.method: VLT-MUSE optical integral field spectroscopy of Ton S180; nuclear spectral modeling with complex permitted-line decomposition and blueshifted [O III] outflow component; custom point spread function subtraction to recover host-galaxy emission; single-epoch estimators combined with stellar velocity dispersion for black hole mass; comparison of observed kinematics with simple inflow models.
AI.result: Black hole mass log(M_BH/M_sun) = 6.5–7.7 and dimensionless mass accretion rate Mdot/Mdot_Edd = 4.1–980, confirming extreme accretion. Host galaxy shows a circumnuclear ring, inner bar-like elongated structure, and rotation-dominated kinematics; inflow models do not significantly improve the fit. A resolved ionized outflow extends ~2 kpc west with v_max~340 km/s and Mdot_out~4.2×10^-4 M_sun/yr, while the unresolved nuclear outflow has v_max~1140 km/s and Mdot_out>1.5 M_sun/yr.
AI.conclusion: Ton S180 is undergoing rapid SMBH growth in an extreme accretion regime, while the observed ionized outflow remains confined to the inner few kiloparsecs and is weak on host-galaxy scales. The contrast between nuclear and resolved outflow properties may reflect weak ionized coupling from nuclear to galactic scales or different episodes of AGN activity over time.

title: Resolved Dust-Gas-Metallicity relations in nearby spiral galaxies
comment: 23 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables. Resubmitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Context: Understanding the interstellar medium (ISM) requires high-resolution, multi-component mapping to capture its complex physical structure. Nearby spiral galaxies, with their abundant and diverse ISM, provide an ideal laboratory for such a comprehensive analysis at sub-galactic scales. Aims: We investigate dust-to-gas (DGR) and dust-to-metal (DMR) ratios as a functions of gas-phase metallicity (Z), on spatial scales ranging from 0.6 to 2.3 kpc, in a sample of 10 nearby spiral galaxies, spanning more than an order of magnitude in stellar mass (9.7 \le \log(M_*/M_\odot) \leq 11.0), star formation rate (SFR, \sim 0.3--3 \, M_\odot \, \rm yr^{-1}) and metallicity ranging from 8.3 \lesssim 12 + \log( O/H) \lesssim 8.8. We explore how the DGR-Z and DMR-Z relations are shaped by the assumptions behind the CO-to-H_2 conversion factor (α_{CO}). Methods: We homogeneously combine maps of dust, atomic gas, molecular gas, and metallicity. Motivated by the diversity in L_{CO(1-0)}/SFR ratios and metallicity across our sample, we introduce a hybrid α_{CO} prescription to distinguish between CO-bright and CO-dark regimes. The derived DGR-Z and DMR-Z relations are compared with other global and resolved observational results, and with the predictions of dust and chemical evolution models. Results: Both DGR-Z and DMR-Z relations are dependent on the adopted α_{CO} prescription, and no single α_{CO} can reproduce the properties of the entire sample, motivating the use of a hybrid approach. The DGR increases with metallicity, spanning \sim 1 dex across the sampled range; while the DMR remains approximately constant at \log(\mathrm{DMR}) = -0.53 \pm 0.13, implying that \sim 30 \% of metals are locked into dust grains. This flat behavior indicates an evolved dust phase where efficient ISM grain growth drives a saturation regime balancing dust formation and destruction.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes dust-to-gas (DGR) and dust-to-metal (DMR) ratios as functions of gas-phase metallicity across 10 nearby spiral galaxies using homogeneous maps of dust, atomic/molecular gas, and metallicity. A hybrid CO-to-H2 conversion factor (α_CO) prescription is introduced to handle both CO-bright and CO-dark regimes. Results show DGR increases ~1 dex with metallicity while DMR remains roughly constant at log(DMR) = -0.53 ± 0.13 (~30% of metals locked in dust), indicating a saturated dust growth regime shaped by grain growth in the ISM.
AI.motivation: The interstellar medium (ISM) presents a complex physical structure that requires high-resolution, multi-component mapping to fully understand. Nearby spiral galaxies—with abundant and diverse ISM content and a wide range of stellar mass, star formation rate, and metallicity—serve as ideal laboratories for studying dust-to-gas and dust-to-metal scaling relations at sub-galactic scales, particularly how these relations depend on assumptions in molecular gas tracing.
AI.method: The authors homogeneously combine maps of dust, atomic gas, molecular gas, and metallicity for 10 nearby spiral galaxies at spatial scales of 0.6–2.3 kpc. A hybrid α_CO prescription is introduced, motivated by observed diversity in L_CO(1-0)/SFR ratios and metallicity, to distinguish CO-bright from CO-dark molecular gas regimes. Derived DGR-Z and DMR-Z relations are then compared against global/resolved observational results and dust and chemical evolution model predictions.
AI.result: Both DGR-Z and DMR-Z relations vary with the assumed α_CO prescription, and no single α_CO value fits the whole sample, supporting the hybrid approach. DGR increases with metallicity spanning ~1 dex across the sampled metallicity range, whereas DMR remains approximately constant at log(DMR) = -0.53 ± 0.13, implying roughly 30% of metals are locked into dust grains. This flat DMR behavior indicates an evolved dust phase where efficient ISM grain growth drives saturation balancing dust formation and destruction.
AI.conclusion: The DGR-Z and DMR-Z relations in nearby spiral galaxies are strongly influenced by molecular gas conversion assumptions, necessitating a hybrid α_CO framework. The constant DMR across a wide metallicity range implies the ISM dust content has reached a saturation regime governed by efficient grain growth balancing formation and destruction, rather than a regime limited purely by metal abundance.

title: AGN-DB: A Unified Multi-Wavelength Database of Active Galactic Nuclei
comment: Submitted to ApJ. Comments and inputs from the community are very welcome!
summary: We present the Active Galactic Nuclei Database (AGN-DB), a comprehensive, multi-wavelength catalog compiled from more than 100 publicly available AGN catalogs and samples released by the end of 2025, spanning radio to $γ$-ray wavelengths. The database contains approximately 8.1 million unique sources, approximately 7.8 million of which remain after flagging stellar contaminants, and approximately 6.8 million of these are classified as AGN. Source cross-matching across catalogs is performed using Lyra, a Bayesian likelihood-ratio framework that jointly considers positional uncertainties, source densities, and photometric information to compute posterior match probabilities. The resulting catalog provides astrometric coordinates, redshifts, photometry, and classifications for each unique source. All multi-catalog provenance is preserved. For every property, we store the full array of values and originating catalog identifiers, enabling multi-epoch and multi-survey analyses. In this paper, we describe the AGN-DB pipeline, including the cross-matching methodology, and present the statistical properties of the v1.0 catalog. AGN-DB is designed to enable population studies, spectral energy distribution modeling, AGN classification, and variability analyses at an unprecedented scale. Its pipeline is designed to facilitate the integration of new catalogs, allowing AGN-DB to be updated regularly, with releases planned at least annually.

AI.tldr: This paper presents AGN-DB, a comprehensive multi-wavelength catalog of approximately 8.1 million unique sources compiled from over 100 public AGN catalogs, cross-matched using the Lyra Bayesian likelihood-ratio framework.
AI.motivation: There is a need for a unified, comprehensive, and multi-wavelength AGN database that aggregates numerous heterogeneous catalogs to enable large-scale population studies and multi-epoch analyses at unprecedented scale.
AI.method: The authors compile data from more than 100 publicly available AGN catalogs released by end of 2025, spanning radio to gamma-ray wavelengths. Cross-matching is performed using Lyra, a Bayesian likelihood-ratio framework that considers positional uncertainties, source densities, and photometric information to compute posterior match probabilities. The pipeline preserves full multi-catalog provenance and stores all property values with originating catalog identifiers.
AI.result: The database contains approximately 8.1 million unique sources, with ~7.8 million remaining after stellar contamination flagging and ~6.8 million classified as AGN. The catalog provides astrometric coordinates, redshifts, photometry, and classifications for each source.
AI.conclusion: AGN-DB enables population studies, spectral energy distribution modeling, AGN classification, and variability analyses at an unprecedented scale. The pipeline is designed for regular updates with releases planned at least annually.

title: Recovering Ionizing Photon Escape and Galaxy Scaling Relations in the LzLCS via Si II and C II Absorption Lines and Mock Spectra from a Radiation-Hydrodynamic Simulation
comment: 20 pages, 8 figures
summary: In this work, we use a radiation-hydrodynamic simulation of a single $\sim10^9M_{\odot}$ virtual galaxy to study Si II and C II line profiles seen in stacked HST/COS spectra of 58 galaxies from the LzLCS+ sample. We compare stacks across three mass bins ($M_{\star} \leq 10^8M_{\odot}$, $10^8$-$10^9M_{\odot}$, and $M_{\star} \geq 10^9M_{\odot}$) and three stacking methods (mean, median, and weighted average) to a library of 22,500 mock spectra. We investigate whether the simulation can accurately mimic real gas features, reveal clear trends with galaxy properties, and provide indirect estimates of the ionizing escape fraction ($f_{\rm esc}$). We find reasonable agreement between simulated and observed profiles ($χ^2 < 1$) across all mass regimes. Notably, extracting line properties such as EW and $R_f$ from best-fit mock profiles provides a robust alternative to direct empirical trends, particularly in the low-S/N regime where noise frequently biases results. The simulation-based LIS features, although derived from a single virtual object, exhibit clear correlations with $M_{\star}$, SFR, and $f_{\rm esc}$, mirroring established empirical scaling relations. We find that the best-matching mock spectra predominantly originate from simulation time steps corresponding to peak UV luminosity and intense starburst phases, suggesting that these active periods generate the ISM diversity observed in star-forming galaxies. Finally, simulation-based estimates ($f_{\rm esc}^{\rm virtual}$) reproduce the observed mass-dependent trends in $f_{\rm esc}$ and are in close agreement with the average $f_{\rm esc}$ of the generated stacks. This simulation-based framework establishes a relevant methodology for interpreting spectroscopic observations, including inferring $f_{\rm esc}$ and characterizing physical scaling relations, in high-redshift galaxies from the Epoch of Reionization.

AI.tldr: This paper uses a radiation-hydrodynamic simulation of a ~10^9 M_sun virtual galaxy to model Si II and C II line profiles observed in stacked HST/COS spectra of 58 LzLCS+ galaxies. Comparing 22,500 mock spectra across mass bins and stacking methods, the simulation reproduces observed profiles (χ² < 1) and provides robust indirect estimates of the ionizing escape fraction (f_esc), which match observed mass-dependent trends.
AI.motivation: To determine whether a single-galaxy radiation-hydrodynamic simulation can accurately reproduce observed low-ionization state (LIS) line profiles in star-forming galaxies, reveal physical trends with galaxy properties, and serve as a reliable framework for inferring ionizing escape fractions—particularly important for interpreting high-redshift galaxies from the Epoch of Reionization.
AI.method: The authors run a radiation-hydrodynamic simulation of a ~10^9 M_sun galaxy and generate 22,500 mock spectra. They compare these to stacked HST/COS spectra of 58 galaxies from the LzLCS+ sample across three stellar mass bins and three stacking methods (mean, median, weighted average). They extract line properties (EW, R_f) from best-fit mock profiles and use them to derive simulation-based f_esc estimates, comparing against empirical trends and observations.
AI.result: Simulated and observed line profiles show reasonable agreement (χ² < 1) across all mass regimes. Extracting line properties from best-fit mock profiles offers a robust alternative to direct empirical trends, especially in low-S/N regimes. The simulated LIS features correlate with M_star, SFR, and f_esc, mirroring empirical scaling relations. Best-matching mock spectra originate predominantly from simulation time steps at peak UV luminosity/starburst phases. Simulation-based f_esc estimates reproduce observed mass-dependent trends and agree with average f_esc of the stacks.
AI.conclusion: This simulation-based framework establishes a viable methodology for interpreting spectroscopic observations—including inferring f_esc and characterizing physical scaling relations—applicable to high-redshift galaxies from the Epoch of Reionization. Despite being derived from a single virtual object, the approach shows broad applicability.

title: The DESI Data Release 1 white dwarf catalogue
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. Catalogue file available at https://cygnus.astro.warwick.ac.uk/phsdaj/WhiteDwarfs/Tables/DESI_DR1_catalogue_1.0.csv.gz
summary: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument is conducting a redshift survey, mapping the universe in three dimensions to measure the history of cosmic expansion. As well as extragalactic objects, it is targeting millions of Milky Way stars, including white dwarfs. Using Data Release 1 we assemble the largest catalogue of spectroscopically-confirmed white dwarfs to date, whose straightforward selection function enables statistically-robust population studies. We visually inspect and fit models to spectra of 63968 objects, finding 44409 white dwarfs. We present their spectral classifications, atmospheric parameters and radial velocities. We assess survey completeness and uniformity, identify potential spectral contamination caused by flux from nearby sources entering the fibre, and assign confidence scores to our classifications to facilitate selection of statistical and observational samples. We present spectra representing most white dwarf classes, common and exotic. We conclude with recommendations and warnings regarding the use of the catalogue.

AI.tldr: The DESI survey, using Data Release 1, has produced the largest catalogue of spectroscopically-confirmed white dwarfs to date, containing 44,409 white dwarfs identified from 63,968 objects, with spectral classifications, atmospheric parameters, and radial velocities provided alongside completeness assessments and quality confidence scores.
AI.motivation: To leverage the DESI redshift survey's observations of millions of Milky Way stars to construct the largest, statistically-robust catalogue of spectroscopically-confirmed white dwarfs, enabling well-grounded population studies that were previously limited by smaller or less uniformly-selected samples.
AI.method: Visual inspection and model fitting of spectra from 63,968 objects selected from DESI Data Release 1, producing classifications, atmospheric parameters, and radial velocities. Survey completeness and uniformity were assessed, fiber contamination from nearby sources was identified, and confidence scores were assigned to facilitate sample selection.
AI.result: A catalogue of 44,409 spectroscopically-confirmed white dwarfs was assembled, representing most white dwarf classes including common and exotic types, together with completeness/uniformity assessments and confidence scores. The catalogue is the largest of its kind to date.
AI.conclusion: The catalogue provides a powerful resource for statistical white dwarf population studies, with recommendations and warnings provided regarding its appropriate use given the selection function, contamination, and classification confidence caveats.

title: Widespread Inflows Reveal Baryonic Cycling in Star-forming and Quiescent Galaxies
comment: 73 pages, 25 Figures (5 Main + 8 Extended Data + 12 Supplementary), submitted on 6th March 2026
summary: Cool-gas inflows, required to sustain star formation, have been fundamental in simulations yet remained observationally elusive. Using DESI spectroscopy of ~30,000 galaxies, we identify coherent inflowing gas (~100 km/s) in 20-50% of the sample, yielding a population-level census of gas flows. We uncover a striking inversion: inflows are detected in quiescent galaxies, whereas star-forming systems are dominated by gravitationally bound outflows. At fixed age, galaxies with inflows, outflows, or no/weak flows share similar masses, environments, and structures, indicating that these properties do not differentiate flow states. Instead, gas-flow state is linked to stellar population age and recent evolutionary history, consistent with age-dependent gas flows in two regimes. In some star-forming galaxies, elevated star formation surface densities drive outflows that recycle on ~0.5 Gyr timescales, consistent with a galactic fountain. In quiescent systems, low-level ``drizzling'' inflows persist, consistent with slowly cooling enriched halo gas and weak radio-mode nuclear activity. Broad gas-phase metallicity distributions---and absence of a pristine dilution signature---indicate that detected inflows are predominantly recycled or enriched. Detectability is modulated by dust, ionization, and geometry: in star-forming disks, inflowing gas lies near the disk plane and is obscured or ionized, while outflow hosts exhibit higher dust and metal content. As star formation declines, cold-outflow signatures weaken, and recycled or slowly cooling gas is more readily detected as inflow. Post-starburst galaxies provide snapshots of this transition. Our results resolve the scarcity of observed inflows, provide evidence for widespread gas accretion and recycling in present day galaxies, and establish an observational framework linking gas flows to star formation, chemical evolution, and galaxy structure.

AI.tldr: Using DESI spectroscopy of ~30,000 galaxies, this paper provides a population-level census of gas flows, revealing that inflows (~100 km/s) are detected in 20-50% of galaxies and are predominantly found in quiescent systems, while star-forming galaxies show gravitationally bound outflows consistent with a galactic fountain. Gas-flow state is linked to stellar population age and recent evolutionary history rather than mass, environment, or structure.
AI.motivation: Cool-gas inflows required to sustain star formation have been fundamental in simulations but have remained observationally elusive. The authors aim to resolve this scarcity of observed inflows and provide an observational census of gas flows across galaxy populations.
AI.method: Analysis of DESI spectroscopy of ~30,000 galaxies to identify coherent inflowing and outflowing gas (~100 km/s), examining flow detections across galaxy properties including star formation state, stellar age, mass, environment, and structure, plus gas-phase metallicity distributions.
AI.result: Inflows are detected in 20-50% of galaxies, with a striking inversion: inflows dominate quiescent galaxies while star-forming systems show gravitationally bound outflows. At fixed age, flow state is independent of mass, environment, and structure. Star-forming galaxies exhibit outflows recycling on ~0.5 Gyr timescales (galactic fountain), while quiescent systems show low-level 'drizzling' inflows from cooling halo gas. Metallicity distributions indicate inflows are predominantly recycled or enriched. Detectability is modulated by dust, ionization, and geometry.
AI.conclusion: The results resolve the observational scarcity of inflows, provide evidence for widespread gas accretion and recycling in present-day galaxies, and establish an observational framework linking gas flows to star formation, chemical evolution, and galaxy structure.

title: Improvements to Asteroseismic Fitting of White Dwarfs in the Gaia Era
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal. 20 pages, 13 figures
summary: White dwarf asteroseismology aims to constrain the interior structures of pulsating white dwarf stars by fitting observed pulsation periods to those computed for stellar models. However, there remain several obstacles for achieving reliable results with the model grid-fitting approach. We simulate data for a parameter recovery experiment in one and two dimensions (mass and effective temperature) to demonstrate improved methodologies that address challenges for characterizing degenerate asteroseismic solutions. We show that interpolating model periods onto a finer grid can adequately resolve asteroseismic solutions that would be missed with sparse model grids. Incorporating absolute magnitude from Gaia astrometry into the statistical fitting is shown to reduce solution degeneracy. We define a seismic solution as a solution to the mode identification problem, and we show that fitting to consistent model pulsation modes can isolate each candidate solution in degenerate solution space. A criterion based on $χ^2$ for what should be considered a reasonable fit is adopted, and we identify all combinations of model periods that meet this criterion, not only those nearest to the measured periods. Finally, we demonstrate how fitting Gaussians to probability distributions allows for the robust characterization of each candidate solution, including uncertainties. Our accurate characterization of the degenerate solution landscape is supported by the comparison of our solutions to a direct marginalization of the likelihood function. These fitting approaches can be generalized to higher dimensions, where there are more than two free parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper develops improved methodologies for white dwarf asteroseismology model grid-fitting, addressing challenges in characterizing degenerate asteroseismic solutions through finer grid interpolation, incorporation of Gaia absolute magnitudes, consistent mode identification, χ²-based solution selection, and Gaussian probability distribution fitting for robust solution characterization.
AI.motivation: White dwarf asteroseismology aims to constrain stellar interior structures by fitting observed pulsation periods to model predictions, but the model grid-fitting approach faces obstacles—particularly solution degeneracy and the risk of missing viable solutions with sparse model grids—that prevent reliable results.
AI.method: The authors simulate data for parameter recovery experiments in one and two dimensions (mass and effective temperature). They implement several methodological improvements: (1) interpolating model periods onto finer grids to resolve solutions missed by sparse grids, (2) incorporating Gaia astrometry-derived absolute magnitudes into the statistical fitting to reduce solution degeneracy, (3) fitting consistent model pulsation modes to isolate each candidate solution in degenerate space, (4) adopting a χ²-based criterion to identify all model period combinations meeting a reasonable-fit threshold (not just nearest to measured periods), and (5) fitting Gaussians to probability distributions for robust characterization of each candidate solution with uncertainties. Results are validated by comparison to direct marginalization of the likelihood function.
AI.result: The parameter recovery experiments demonstrate that each proposed methodology effectively addresses its targeted challenge: fine grid interpolation recovers seismic solutions that sparse grids would miss, Gaia absolute magnitudes reduce solution degeneracy, consistent mode fitting isolates individual candidate solutions, the χ² criterion identifies all acceptable solutions, and Gaussian fitting provides robust characterizations with uncertainties that match direct likelihood marginalization results.
AI.conclusion: The improved fitting methodologies enable accurate characterization of the degenerate solution landscape in white dwarf asteroseismology, and these approaches can be generalized to higher-dimensional parameter spaces with more than two free parameters.

title: H I Absorbers as Beacons of Hidden Structure at $z \sim 3$: Multi-Component, Metal-Rich Absorption System near a Protocluster
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 17 pages, 19 figures
summary: H I gas traces the large-scale structure and provides the primary fuel for star formation. High-$z$ protoclusters are ideal laboratories to study how H I gas is accreted and consumed during the formation of the most massive structures in the Universe. However, much remains unknown about the distribution and physical state of their H I gas. We examine a rare configuration in which a protocluster candidate is located in front of a quasar at $z=3.09$. Our spectroscopic campaign confirms a protocluster at $z=3.079$: however, no corresponding strong H I absorption is found in the background quasar spectrum. Instead, we serendipitously discover a prominent H I absorption feature at $z\sim 3.01$, offset by $\sim 60$ cMpc from the centre of the protocluster. Spanning an exceptionally broad velocity range of $\sim 2000$ km s$^{-1}$ ($\sim 40$ cMpc), this absorption is decoupled from the confirmed member galaxies. Detailed kinematic modelling reveals this absorption comprises five distinct components rather than a single cloud. Moreover, one of these components exhibits a super-solar metallicity ($[\mathrm{O/H}] = +1.19^{+0.91}_{-0.78}$). We propose two physical scenarios for this unique system: (1) an additional, hidden massive protocluster along the line of sight, and/or (2) metal-rich outflows and metal-poor inflows driven by a single massive galaxy. The discovery highlights that while protoclusters are not universally associated with strong H I absorption, targeting the strong H I absorbers may serve as a beacon for uncovering massive, metal-rich protoclusters or complex gas kinematics in the early Universe.

AI.tldr: This paper examines a protocluster candidate at z=3.079 located in front of a background quasar at z=3.09, using the background quasar as a probe of the protocluster's HI gas. Surprisingly, no strong HI absorption is found associated with the protocluster itself; instead, a broad (~2000 km/s), five-component HI absorption system is serendipitously discovered at z~3.01, offset ~60 cMpc from the protocluster center, with one component showing super-solar metallicity ([O/H]=+1.19). Two scenarios are proposed: a hidden massive protocluster along the line of sight, or metal-rich outflows/inflows from a single massive galaxy.
AI.motivation: High-z protoclusters are ideal laboratories for studying how HI gas is accreted and consumed during the formation of the most massive structures in the Universe, yet little is known about the distribution and physical state of HI gas in these environments. This rare configuration—a protocluster in front of a background quasar—provides a unique opportunity to probe HI gas around protocluster candidates via absorption spectroscopy.
AI.method: A spectroscopic campaign was conducted to confirm a protocluster at z=3.079 in front of a background quasar at z=3.09. The quasar's spectrum was used to search for associated HI absorption from the protocluster. Detailed kinematic modelling of any detected absorption features was performed to decompose the absorption profile into its constituent velocity components.
AI.result: The protocluster was confirmed at z=3.079, but no strong HI absorption was found at its redshift in the background quasar spectrum. Instead, a prominent, exceptionally broad (~2000 km/s, ~40 cMpc) HI absorption feature was discovered at z~3.01, offset ~60 cMpc from the protocluster center and decoupled from confirmed member galaxies. Kinematic modelling shows this absorption comprises five distinct components, one of which exhibits super-solar metallicity ([O/H]=+1.19).
AI.conclusion: Protoclusters are not universally associated with strong HI absorption. However, strong HI absorbers in the early Universe may serve as beacons for uncovering massive, metal-rich protoclusters or complex gas kinematics (outflows/inflows associated with massive galaxies) not otherwise detected.

title: Can isolated binaries form unequal-mass binary black-hole mergers with a high-spin primary black hole?
comment: submitted
summary: GWTC-5 has revealed a subpopulation of merging binary black holes (BBHs) with a high-spin primary black hole (BH) and possibly unequal BH masses. GW241110 additionally exhibits a large spin-orbit misalignment, which suggests a hierarchical-merger origin. However, other formation scenarios are possible or even likely, especially for events without constraints on spin-orbit misalignment. As an alternative to hierarchical mergers, we investigate whether binary evolution can produce unequal-mass BBH mergers with a high-spin primary BH. Rather than performing comprehensive population-synthesis calculations, we examine the evolutionary pathways of forming merging BBHs and assess their uncertainties. We identify two possible pathways for producing unequal-mass BBHs with a high-spin primary. In initially wide binaries, mass-ratio reversal can make the tidally spun-up second-born BH both more massive and more rapidly rotating than the first-born BH; alternatively, in an initially close, unequal-mass binary, the primary star may evolve chemically homogeneously, while the secondary star evolves normally, producing a high-spin first-born BH that is more massive than its companion. Generally, large spin-orbit misalignment can be produced by large natal kicks or tertiary-induced nodal precession and/or Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai oscillations. We conclude that hierarchical mergers are not uniquely required to produce unequal-mass BBHs with a high-spin primary BH, although each isolated-binary pathway faces important theoretical constraints. Future detections of more merger events with primary BH spins around 0.7 would discriminate between binary evolution and hierarchical merger origin.

AI.tldr: The authors investigate whether isolated binary evolution can produce unequal-mass BBH mergers with high-spin primary BHs, as an alternative to hierarchical mergers. They identify two evolutionary pathways (mass-ratio reversal in wide binaries, or chemically homogeneous evolution in close binaries) that can produce such systems, and conclude that hierarchical mergers are not uniquely required, though each pathway faces theoretical constraints.
AI.motivation: GWTC-5 has revealed a subpopulation of merging BBHs with high-spin primary BHs and possibly unequal masses. GW241110 exhibits large spin-orbit misalignment suggesting hierarchical-merger origin, but other formation scenarios are possible or even likely, especially for events without spin-orbit misalignment constraints. This motivates investigating whether isolated binary evolution can produce such systems as an alternative.
AI.method: Rather than performing comprehensive population-synthesis calculations, the authors examine the evolutionary pathways of forming merging BBHs and assess their uncertainties. They investigate two possible pathways: (1) mass-ratio reversal in initially wide binaries making the tidally spun-up second-born BH more massive and rapidly rotating than the first-born BH; (2) chemically homogeneous evolution of the primary star in an initially close unequal-mass binary while the secondary evolves normally. They also discuss mechanisms for producing large spin-orbit misalignment including large natal kicks and tertiary-induced nodal precession/Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai oscillations.
AI.result: The authors identify two viable isolated-binary pathways capable of producing unequal-mass BBHs with high-spin primary BHs. Large spin-orbit misalignment can be produced through large natal kicks or tertiary-induced dynamical effects. Each pathway faces important theoretical constraints, and future detections of merger events with primary BH spins around 0.7 would help discriminate between binary evolution and hierarchical merger origin.
AI.conclusion: Hierarchical mergers are not uniquely required to produce unequal-mass BBHs with a high-spin primary BH. Isolated binary evolution offers viable alternative pathways, though they face theoretical constraints. Future observations of events with primary spins around 0.7 will be key to distinguishing between these formation scenarios.

title: Extending the Stellar-to-Halo Mass Relation to Dwarf Galaxies with DESI DR1
comment: 23 pages (+4 pages of appendices), 11 figures. Comments are welcome!
summary: Constraining the dark matter halos of the smallest galaxies offers fundamental insights into the nature of dark matter and stellar feedback. Using the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Data Release 1, we infer the stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR) down to the dwarf scale ($M_\star < 10^9\,M_\odot$), without extrapolation from the higher mass range. Leveraging the unprecedented depth of the DESI Bright Galaxy Survey at $0.01 < z < 0.2$, we construct 12 samples spanning nearly four orders of magnitude in stellar mass, and measure their projected clustering $w_p$, galaxy-galaxy lensing $ΔΣ$, as well as a novel observable: satellite occupation number $N_{\rm sat}$. The addition of $N_{\rm sat}$ enables robust subtraction of satellite contributions to both $w_p$ and $ΔΣ$ across the 12 individual halo occupation distribution analyses, yielding an average halo-to-stellar mass relation (HSMR) of $\log \langle M_h(M_\star) \rangle = 12.06 + 0.58\log(M_\star/10^{11}) + (M_\star/10^{11})^{0.73}$. Combining this HSMR with an observed stellar mass function, we constrain the SHMR across five orders of magnitude in halo mass, with the power-law slope steepening from $0.32 \pm 0.06$ above the Milky Way mass to $2.08 \pm 0.21$ in the dwarf regime. Interestingly, the scatter about the SHMR grows from $0.17 \pm 0.02$ dex at Milky Way-like scales to $0.68_{-0.33}^{+0.21}$ dex for systems comparable to the Large Magellanic Cloud, suggesting that smaller galaxies follow increasingly diverse evolutionary paths. Our work highlights the power of DESI in probing the galaxy-halo connection within the dwarf regime, offering an exciting avenue to bridge the gap between large-scale and near-field cosmologies in the future.

They find a steepening SHMR power-law slope (from 0.32 at Milky Way scales to 2.08 in the dwarf regime) and increasing scatter at smaller masses, highlighting DESI's power for probing the galaxy-halo connection in dwarfs.

AI.method: Using DESI Bright Galaxy Survey data (0.01<z<0.2), the authors construct 12 galaxy samples spanning ~4 orders of magnitude in stellar mass. Nsat enables robust subtraction of satellite contributions in 12 individual halo occupation distribution analyses.
