title: Energy Partitioning at the Termination Shock
summary: We show new results of a global 3D magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulation of the Boston University outer heliosphere model where we used a newly developed approach that distributes the non-adiabatic shock heating among the cold protons, electrons, and pickup-ions (PUIs), while maintaining total energy conservation of all ions (cold protons and PUIs) and electrons. In our previous simulations ( E.S. Bair et al. 2025; B. van der Holst et al. 2026), all non-adiabatic shock heating was channeled to the cold protons, resulting in a too large temperature jump at the termination shock (TS) for the thermal solar wind. Using a new methodology we improved the simulation results with respect to the temperature jump observed at the TS by Voyager 2 (V2) spacecraft. Our simulations approached the observed jump conditions of a factor 10--20 in the cold solar wind temperature V2 measurements, and we obtain improvements in the simulation results relative to the data. Because we directly estimate in this way the distribution of non-adiabatic heating at the TS, we have the opportunity to study the physical process of heating cold plasma and PUIs in the TS. The results show that having almost 100\% non-adiabatic shock heating going towards PUIs at the TS reproduces the jump conditions observed along the V2 trajectory. This information is key to understanding the physical processes that shape the heliosphere. As shown by M. Opher et al. (2020), PUIs significantly change the shape of the heliosphere, for example, the presence of hot PUIs results in a deflated inner heliosheath. Our work provides the architecture of how energy partitioning at shocks in kinetic simulations (J. Giacalone et al. 2021) can be utilized in global MHD models.

AI.tldr: This paper presents improved global 3D MHD simulations of the outer heliosphere using a new approach that distributes non-adiabatic shock heating among cold protons, electrons, and pickup-ions (PUIs) while conserving total energy. By channeling nearly 100% of shock heating to PUIs at the termination shock (TS), the simulations successfully reproduce the factor 10-20 temperature jump observed by Voyager 2, correcting previous models that allocated all heating to cold protons.
AI.motivation: Previous simulations by Bair et al. (2025) and van der Holst et al. (2026) channeled all non-adiabatic shock heating to cold protons, producing excessively large temperature jumps at the termination shock compared to Voyager 2 observations. The aim is to correctly partition energy among plasma components to match observational data and understand the physics of shock heating in the heliosphere.
AI.method: The authors developed a new methodology for the Boston University outer heliosphere model that distributes non-adiabatic shock heating among cold protons, electrons, and PUIs while ensuring total energy conservation across all ions and electrons. They ran global 3D MHD simulations testing different energy partition schemes and compared results to Voyager 2 measurements of the temperature jump at the termination shock.
AI.result: Distributing almost 100% of non-adiabatic shock heating to PUIs at the TS reproduces the observed factor 10-20 temperature jump in the cold solar wind along the V2 trajectory. This approach yields significant improvements in simulation results relative to observational data compared to previous models.
AI.conclusion: PUIs receive the dominant share of shock heating at the termination shock, which is key to understanding heliospheric structure. The work demonstrates how energy partitioning at shocks from kinetic simulations (Giacalone et al. 2021) can be incorporated into global MHD models, providing a framework for connecting microphysics to global heliospheric simulations.

title: Hint of bimodal Mg-Al anticorrelation in the metal-poor Globular Cluster NGC 4372
comment: 11 pages, 12 figures
summary: We present a detailed chemical abundance analysis of seven red giant branch stars in the very metal-poor globular cluster NGC~4372, based on high-resolution UVES spectra. Our study aims to characterize the chemical evolution of NGC~4372 and investigate the presence of multiple populations. We derived abundances for 17 elements, including light, iron-peak, $α$, and heavy elements, using both equivalent width and spectral synthesis methods. We find a mean cluster metallicity of [Fe/H]=$-$2.36 $\pm$ 0.03 dex, with no evidence of an intrinsic iron spread. The cluster exhibits a typical $α$-enhancement of [$α$/Fe]= 0.33 $\pm$ 0.05 dex and a well defined Na-O anticorrelation, confirming that NGC 4372 hosts at least two distinct stellar populations. Furthermore, the measured ratio of [Ba/Eu] =$-0.47 \pm 0.04$ indicates that the synthesis of heavy elements was dominated by $r$-process, consistent with other very metal-poor environments. We also identify a potential bimodal Mg-Al anticorrelation, which aligns with the patterns observed in GCs of similar mass and metallicity. These results reinforce the status of NGC 4372 as a cornerstone for understanding the early chemical enrichment of the Galactic Halo.

AI.tldr: A detailed chemical abundance analysis of seven red giant branch stars in the very metal-poor globular cluster NGC 4372 using high-resolution UVES spectra, finding [Fe/H]=-2.36±0.03, α-enhancement of 0.33±0.05, evidence of multiple stellar populations via Na-O anticorrelation, and r-process-dominated heavy element synthesis.
AI.motivation: To characterize the chemical evolution of NGC 4372, a very metal-poor globular cluster, and investigate the presence of multiple stellar populations to better understand early chemical enrichment of the Galactic Halo.
AI.method: High-resolution UVES spectroscopy of seven red giant branch stars in NGC 4372, with abundance derivations for 17 elements (light, iron-peak, α, and heavy elements) using both equivalent width and spectral synthesis methods.
AI.result: Mean metallicity [Fe/H]=-2.36±0.03 dex with no intrinsic iron spread; typical α-enhancement of 0.33±0.05 dex; well-defined Na-O anticorrelation confirming at least two stellar populations; [Ba/Eu]=-0.47±0.04 indicating r-process dominance; potential bimodal Mg-Al anticorrelation consistent with similar globular clusters.
AI.conclusion: NGC 4372 hosts multiple stellar populations, exhibits r-process-dominated heavy element synthesis typical of very metal-poor environments, and serves as a cornerstone for understanding the early chemical enrichment of the Galactic Halo.

title: ROCKETS I: Investigating the Impact of the Rocket Effect on Two Nearby Young Open Clusters Encased in Infrared Bubbles
comment: 13 Pages, 10 Figures, 1 Table, accepted for publication in Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia
summary: We introduce ROCKETS (Rocket-driven Cluster Kinematics & Triggered Star-formation), a Gaia based programme investigating kinematic fingerprints of stellar feedback or rocket effect in young star forming regions. We analyse two young clusters with O-type stars enclosed by mid-infrared bubbles, Collinder 69 and IC 1396 as a methodological demonstration on two nearby benchmark regions. Co-moving candidates are selected within an astrometric ellipse defined by the median and median absolute deviation of Class I/II YSOs with Gaia data. For each star, we compute a relative proper-motion angle (RPMA) relative to the ionising source. In both regions the RPMA distribution shows a strong excess at RPMA $<15^{\circ}$, corresponding to sources moving away from the respective ionising sources. We quantify this using the Rocket Effect Index (REI), finding $\mathrm{REI}\simeq 1.1$ for Collinder 69 and $\mathrm{REI}\simeq 1.7$ for IC 1396. When considering only Class I/II YSOs, the REI of both regions increases to $\mathrm{REI}\gtrsim 10$. Velocity-structure analysis of the sample shows that the RPMA $<15^\circ$ subset has stronger positive pairwise expansion than the full co-moving population, providing additional support for the rocket effect. The outward-moving stars are not uniformly distributed; instead, their position angles are strongly anisotropic and preferentially aligned towards the bright-rimmed clouds. Gaia colour-magnitude diagrams show no strong age offset between sources moving outward and literature cluster members. The observed kinematic signatures support feedback-driven acceleration of gas and triggered star formation preferentially towards higher density regions of expanding bubbles due to the rocket effect.

AI.tldr: ROCKETS is a Gaia-based program studying kinematic signatures of stellar feedback ("rocket effect") in young clusters. Analyzing Collinder 69 and IC 1396, the authors find strong excess of stars moving away from ionising sources (RPMA<15°), quantified by Rocket Effect Index values of ~1.1 and ~1.7 respectively (increasing to ≥10 for Class I/II YSOs only). Velocity-structure analysis confirms positive pairwise expansion among outward-moving stars, which are anisotropically aligned toward bright-rimmed clouds, supporting feedback-driven acceleration and triggered star formation in expanding bubbles.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether stellar feedback from O-type stars kinematically accelerates surrounding gas and triggers star formation in young clusters—the so-called "rocket effect"—using Gaia astrometry to identify and quantify these kinematic fingerprints.
AI.method: Using Gaia astrometry, co-moving candidates are selected via an astrometric ellipse based on median and MAD of Class I/II YSOs. For each star, a relative proper-motion angle (RPMA) relative to the ionising source is computed. The Rocket Effect Index (REI) quantifies the excess of outward-moving sources. Pairwise expansion analysis and position-angle anisotropy tests are applied, along with Gaia color-magnitude diagrams to assess age differences.
AI.result: Both regions show a strong RPMA excess at <15° (outward-moving sources), with REI≈1.1 (Collinder 69) and REI≈1.7 (IC 1396), increasing to ≳10 when restricted to Class I/II YSOs. Outward-moving stars exhibit stronger positive pairwise expansion and are anisotropically aligned toward bright-rimmed clouds. No significant age offset is found between outward-moving sources and literature cluster members.
AI.conclusion: The kinematic signatures observed provide evidence for feedback-driven (rocket effect) acceleration of gas and triggered star formation, preferentially directed toward higher-density regions of expanding bubbles around O-type stars.

title: Linking orbital history to the quenching of isolated dwarf galaxies
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, submitted to OJAp, comments welcome
summary: Recent discoveries of isolated dwarf galaxies (${M}_{\star}\sim 10^{7-9}~{\rm M}_{\odot}$) with no signs of ongoing star formation have challenged the prevailing notion that these solitary systems are exclusively star-forming. Investigating the origins of isolated quenched dwarfs provides important clues into the dominant processes driving galaxy quenching as a function of environment and stellar mass. In this study, we identify central dwarf galaxies in the Illustris-TNG50 cosmological simulation with ${M}_{\star} \sim 10^{7-9}~{\rm M}_{\odot}$, evaluate their star formation and orbital histories, and investigate how their dark matter halo properties correlate with quenching and interactions with massive neighbors. We find that $R_{\rm{peri}}$, defined as the closest separation ever attained between a central dwarf and a galaxy more massive than ${M}_{\star}> 10^{10}~{\rm M}_{\odot}$, is a reliable metric for inferring the star formation history of central dwarfs in TNG50. We also show that isolated quenched dwarf galaxies separate into backsplash and non-backsplash subpopulations as a function of $R_{\rm{peri}}$, and that non-backsplash galaxies are consistent with being quenched by cosmic web stripping or internal feedback mechanisms. Furthermore, we find that $R_{\rm{peri}}$ correlates strongly with dark matter halo mass and star formation proxies based on halo maximum circular velocity, which are commonly used in empirical galaxy-halo connection models. These predictions can be tested with data from upcoming deep and wide surveys (e.g., Rubin LSST and Roman) that are anticipated to significantly increase the cosmic census of dwarf galaxies.

AI.tldr: Using the Illustris-TNG50 cosmological simulation, the study identifies central dwarf galaxies (M⋆ ~ 10^7-9 M⊙) and finds that R_peri—the closest approach to a massive neighbor (M⋆ > 10^10 M⊙)—is a reliable metric for predicting the star formation history of central dwarfs. Isolated quenched dwarfs separate into backsplash and non-backsplash populations, with the latter quenched by cosmic web stripping or internal feedback. R_peri also correlates with halo mass and maximum circular velocity proxies used in galaxy-halo connection models.
AI.motivation: The discovery of isolated dwarf galaxies with no ongoing star formation challenges the assumption that solitary dwarfs are exclusively star-forming. Understanding the origins of these isolated quenched dwarfs provides insights into the dominant quenching processes as functions of environment and stellar mass.
AI.method: The authors analyze central dwarf galaxies in the Illustris-TNG50 cosmological simulation with stellar masses of 10^7-9 M⊙. They evaluate star formation and orbital histories, and study correlations between dark matter halo properties and quenching, using R_peri (the minimum separation ever achieved from a galaxy more massive than 10^10 M⊙) as a key diagnostic metric.
AI.result: R_peri is a reliable predictor of central dwarf star formation history in TNG50. Isolated quenched dwarfs separate into backsplash and non-backsplash subpopulations based on R_peri; non-backsplash dwarfs are quenched by cosmic web stripping or internal feedback. R_peri strongly correlates with dark matter halo mass and star formation proxies based on halo maximum circular velocity.
AI.conclusion: The predictions linking dwarf quenching to orbital and halo properties can be tested with future deep and wide surveys such as Rubin LSST and Roman, which will substantially increase the census of dwarf galaxies in the universe.

title: KKR 18: A Late Arrival Galaxy?
comment: 12 pages, 13 figures. Submitted to The Astrophysical Journal
summary: KKR 18 is a dwarf irregular galaxy in the Local Void at a distance of 9.46 Mpc. It is gas rich and was experiencing vigorous star formation 20 - 100 Myr ago. Its metallicity is 4% of Solar from an emission spectrum, qualifying is as extremely metal poor (XMP). Its most remarkable characteristic is an extremely deficient Red Giant Branch. This feature is shared with a small number of other dwarf galaxies and it is inferred that they lack ancient stellar components. It is suggested that these are late arrival galaxies (LAG).

AI.tldr: KKR 18 is a dwarf irregular galaxy in the Local Void at 9.46 Mpc, characterized by a gas-rich composition, recent intense star formation (20-100 Myr ago), extremely low metallicity (4% Solar), and a notably deficient Red Giant Branch, suggesting it lacks ancient stellar populations and may be a late arrival galaxy (LAG).
AI.motivation: To characterize KKR 18, an unusual dwarf irregular galaxy whose properties may provide insight into galaxy formation and evolution, particularly regarding galaxies lacking ancient stellar components.
AI.method: The study analyzes KKR 18's stellar populations, gas content, metallicity from emission spectra, and star formation history, with emphasis on the deficiency in the Red Giant Branch.
AI.result: KKR 18 is an extremely metal-poor (XMP) dwarf irregular galaxy with 4% Solar metallicity, gas-rich, having experienced vigorous star formation 20-100 Myr ago, and displaying a very deficient Red Giant Branch implying no ancient stellar populations.
AI.conclusion: KKR 18, like a few other dwarf galaxies with deficient Red Giant Branches, likely lacks ancient stellar components and is proposed to be a late arrival galaxy (LAG).

title: Membership Determination of 45 Open Clusters Beyond 3 kpc
comment: 14 pages, accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Context. Open clusters (OCs) are fundamental tracers for studying the structure and chemical evolution of the Galactic disc. Reliable identification of cluster members, particularly at the faint end of the main sequence, remains challenging owing to severe field-star contamination and the declining photometric completeness for distant, obscured systems. Aims. We aim to identify and characterise distant OC candidates at heliocentric distances $d \gtrsim 3$ kpc using Gaia DR3 astrometry, with emphasis on improving the recovery of faint candidate members in highly contaminated stellar fields. Methods. We apply a probabilistic membership method based on Gaia DR3 proper motions and parallaxes. Candidate members are selected through combined astrometric criteria and refined via spatial filtering using radial density profiles, with photometric data serving as a consistency check. For clusters affected by significant extinction, near-infrared photometry from 2MASS is incorporated to compensate for the limitations of optical data. Results. We analyse a sample of 45 targets, comprising 30 previously reported OCs and 15 newly identified candidates, all located at $d \gtrsim 3$ kpc. The method yields more compact astrometric distributions and improves the recovery of faint candidate members in several systems. However, residual field contamination remains non-negligible for the most obscured clusters projected against the Galactic plane. Conclusions. Gaia DR3 astrometry provides an effective basis for the exploratory identification and first-order characterisation of distant OC candidates. Dedicated near-infrared follow-up observations will be essential for robust membership assessment in high extincted regions.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a probabilistic membership method using Gaia DR3 proper motions and parallaxes to identify and characterize distant open clusters (d ≥ 3 kpc), tested on 45 targets (30 known OCs and 15 new candidates). The method improves faint member recovery and yields more compact astrometric distributions, though residual field contamination persists for heavily obscured clusters near the Galactic plane.
AI.motivation: Open clusters are key tracers for studying Galactic disc structure and chemical evolution, but reliable member identification at the faint main-sequence end is difficult due to field-star contamination and declining photometric completeness for distant, obscured systems. The goal is to reliably identify distant OC candidates at d ≥ 3 kpc using Gaia DR3 astrometry.
AI.method: A probabilistic membership method based on Gaia DR3 proper motions and parallaxes is applied. Candidate members are selected via combined astrometric criteria, refined with spatial filtering using radial density profiles, and cross-checked with photometry. For clusters with significant extinction, 2MASS near-infrared photometry supplements the limited optical data.
AI.result: Analysis of 45 targets (30 previously reported OCs and 15 new candidates at d ≥ 3 kpc) shows the method produces more compact astrometric distributions and improves recovery of faint candidate members in several systems. However, residual field contamination remains non-negligible for the most obscured clusters projected against the Galactic plane.
AI.conclusion: Gaia DR3 astrometry is an effective basis for exploratory identification and first-order characterization of distant OC candidates. Dedicated near-infrared follow-up observations are essential for robust membership assessment in highly extincted regions.

title: Star Formation Evolution in Galaxy Pairs: Constraints from Morphological Disturbances and Recent Star Formation Histories
comment: 20 pages, 8 figures; accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: Galaxy interactions can enhance star formation, but how star formation evolves during galaxy interactions remains poorly constrained by observations. We combine pair separation, morphological disturbance, and recent star formation history to study this evolution. We measure morphological disturbance with the shape asymmetry parameter ($A_{\rm shape}$) using deep images from the DESI Legacy Surveys, and use Galaxy Zoo DESI classifications as an independent test. We infer recent star formation histories by comparing SFR and $\mathrm{EW}(\mathrm{H}α)$, which trace current star formation, with $\mathrm{EW}(\mathrm{H}δ_A)$ and $D_n4000$, which are sensitive to stellar populations formed over longer timescales. At small projected separations, strongly disturbed galaxies show the strongest enhancements in SFR and $\mathrm{EW}(\mathrm{H}α)$, indicating that close encounters trigger strong star formation. At intermediate separations ($d_{\rm p}\sim100\,\mathrm{kpc}$), their current star formation is only moderately enhanced, but their $\mathrm{EW}(\mathrm{H}δ_A)$ enhancement is the strongest. This indicates a larger contribution from intermediate-age stars formed during stronger star formation in the past $\sim0.1$--$1\,\mathrm{Gyr}$. The TNG100 analysis shows that this pattern results from rapid changes in SFR around close passage. SFR rises sharply during the encounter and declines as the galaxies move apart, while tidal disturbances remain visible. As short-lived massive stars disappear and intermediate-age A-type stars begin to dominate the spectrum, the $\mathrm{EW}(\mathrm{H}δ_A)$ enhancement peaks later than the SFR enhancement. Our results provide important observational evidence for the evolution of SFR along the merger sequence.

AI.tldr: This study combines pair separation, morphological disturbance (A_shape), and recent star formation history indicators to track how star formation evolves during galaxy interactions. They find that strongly disturbed galaxies show the strongest SFR enhancement at small separations, while EW(Hδ_A) enhancement peaks at intermediate separations (~100 kpc), indicating star formation peaks near close passage and then declines while tidal disturbance signatures persist.
AI.motivation: Although galaxy interactions are known to enhance star formation, its temporal evolution during the interaction process remains poorly constrained by observations. Existing observational studies have lacked the combination of merger stage indicators and SFH-sensitive tracers to map out the full evolution.
AI.method: The authors use pair separation, morphological disturbance (measured via the shape asymmetry parameter A_shape from DESI Legacy Surveys deep images, validated with Galaxy Zoo DESI classifications), and multi-timescale star formation indicators: SFR and EW(Hα) trace ongoing star formation, while EW(Hδ_A) and D_n4000 probe stellar populations formed over 0.1-1 Gyr timescales. They complement the observations with TNG100 simulations to explain the physical picture.
AI.result: Strongly disturbed galaxies show the largest SFR and EW(Hα) enhancements at small projected separations, indicating close encounters trigger strong star formation. At intermediate separations (~100 kpc), current star formation is only moderately enhanced but EW(Hδ_A) enhancement is strongest, implying a peak contribution from intermediate-age stars formed 0.1-1 Gyr earlier. TNG100 simulations confirm this pattern arises from a rapid SFR rise around close passage followed by decline as galaxies separate, with EW(Hδ_A) peaking later than SFR due to the delayed emergence of intermediate-age A-type stars.
AI.conclusion: The observations provide important evidence for how star formation evolves along the merger sequence: star formation peaks during close encounters and subsequently declines, with the stellar population signatures evolving on delayed timescales relative to the SFR itself.

title: Quantifying collision-driven mass loss in supermassive star formation: the role of stellar structure and accretion
summary: Observations of high-redshift galaxies with JWST have renewed interest in scenarios where supermassive stars form via runaway stellar collisions in dense clusters, yet the impact of collision-driven mass loss on their growth remains uncertain. In this work, we perform a post-processing analysis of 3D hydrodynamical simulations of the formation of a supermassive star, applying an analytic mass-loss prescription to stellar collisions while exploring different assumptions for the internal stellar structure. We consider a polytropic main-sequence model, a semi-analytic accreting protostar model, and structures derived from stellar evolution calculations. We find that the cumulative mass-loss fraction depends sensitively on the adopted stellar structure, ranging from $\lesssim 10-25\%$ for more compact configurations to $\gtrsim 30-40\%$ for more extended protostellar models. The importance of mass loss further depends on the dynamical state of the system, including the ratio of stellar velocity dispersion to the stellar surface escape velocity. We find significant uncertainty depending on the prescription used. As a result, collision-driven mass loss could significantly limit the growth of the central object, at least in some cases. Overall, our results indicate that uncertainties in the internal structure of rapidly accreting protostars represent a major source of systematic uncertainty and must be better constrained to robustly assess the viability of runaway-collision pathways for forming massive black hole seeds.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of collision-driven mass loss on supermassive star formation in dense clusters using 3D hydrodynamical simulations with different stellar structure models, finding that mass-loss fractions range from ~10-40% depending on the assumed internal structure, which introduces significant uncertainty in assessing runaway-collision pathways for massive black hole seed formation.
AI.motivation: JWST observations of high-redshift galaxies have renewed interest in supermassive star formation via runaway stellar collisions in dense clusters, but the effect of collision-driven mass loss on stellar growth is poorly constrained, hindering robust assessment of this channel for forming massive black hole seeds.
AI.method: The authors perform post-processing analysis of 3D hydrodynamical simulations of supermassive star formation, applying an analytic mass-loss prescription to stellar collisions. They explore different internal stellar structure assumptions: a polytropic main-sequence model, a semi-analytic accreting protostar model, and structures from stellar evolution calculations.
AI.result: Cumulative mass-loss fraction depends sensitively on stellar structure: less than 10-25% for compact configurations versus greater than 30-40% for extended protostellar models. Mass-loss importance also depends on the system's dynamical state, including the ratio of stellar velocity dispersion to stellar surface escape velocity. Significant prescription-dependent uncertainty is found.
AI.conclusion: Collision-driven mass loss could significantly limit central object growth in some cases. Uncertainties in the internal structure of rapidly accreting protostars are a major source of systematic uncertainty and must be better constrained to robustly assess runaway-collision pathways for forming massive black hole seeds.

title: Rubin J122659.4+090236: An Extremely Low Surface Brightness Galaxy Candidate Discovered in the Rubin LSST Early Data Preview 2
comment: 16 pages (including appendices), 9 figures, 4 tables
summary: We report the serendipitous discovery of an exceptionally low surface brightness galaxy (LSBG) candidate, Rubin J122659.4+090236, in Rubin Observatory imaging of the interacting NGC 4410 system, identified in the Cosmic Treasure Chest public release. 2D Sérsic modelling of the Rubin g, r, and i images reveals a nearly round system with a shallow profile (n ~ 0.4), an effective radius of R_e ~ 6'', and central surface brightnesses of $μ_{0,g}=27.52\pm0.04$, $μ_{0,r}=27.62\pm0.07$, and $μ_{0,i}=27.04\pm0.08$ mag arcsec$^{-2}$. EAZY photo-z fitting favours an intermediate-z solution at z~0.3, while a low-redshift solution at z~0.028, consistent with the NGC 4410 system, is also permitted by a restricted EAZY fit over 0<z<0.1 without imposing a redshift prior. These alternatives imply substantially different physical interpretations, ranging from a diffuse dwarf-like system to an exceptionally extended background LSBG. This discovery demonstrates Rubin's sensitivity to extremely diffuse galaxies and highlights the potential of the LSST survey to uncover large samples of such elusive systems across wide areas, enabling systematic studies of the LSBG population and its role in galaxy evolution.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the serendipitous discovery of an exceptionally low surface brightness galaxy (LSBG) candidate, Rubin J122659.4+090236, found in Rubin Observatory imaging of the interacting NGC 4410 system. Photometric modelling and photo-z fitting reveal ambiguous distance solutions (z~0.3 intermediate-z vs. z~0.028 local), implying radically different physical interpretations. The discovery demonstrates Rubin's sensitivity to extreme diffuse galaxies and the potential of LSST to discover large LSBG samples.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate Rubin Observatory's capability to detect extremely diffuse, low surface brightness galaxies and highlight the potential of LSST surveys for discovering and systematically studying large samples of such elusive systems, which are poorly understood in terms of their role in galaxy evolution.
AI.method: 2D Sérsic profile modelling of Rubin g, r, and i band images to derive structural parameters; EAZY photometric redshift fitting, including both a free fit and a restricted fit over 0<z<0.1 without a redshift prior, to explore the distance ambiguity.
AI.result: The candidate exhibits a nearly round morphology with shallow Sérsic index (n~0.4), effective radius R_e~6'', and central surface brightnesses of ~27.0-27.6 mag arcsec^-2 in g, r, and i bands. EAZY favours z~0.3 but permits z~0.028, leading to two distinct physical scenarios: a diffuse dwarf-like galaxy or an exceptionally extended background LSBG.
AI.conclusion: Rubin Observatory imaging can reveal extremely diffuse galaxies, and with the LSST survey's wide-area coverage, such discoveries can scale to large samples, enabling systematic studies of the LSBG population and its role in galaxy evolution.

title: Corona Australis 151: an extremely young protostar
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A Letters
summary:
Context. Prestellar cores are the birthplace of stars and planetary systems, but they are short-lived objects, since the initial stages of dense core evolution, collapse, and the formation of a protostellar seed are fast. In an effort to build a catalogue of bona-fide prestellar cores in the Solar neighbourhood, we used APEX observations to identify dynamically evolved cores among dense cores observed with Herschel. One of them, Corona Australis 151, stood out because of its centrally peaked structure, with densities above 1e7cm-3 in the central 500-1000 au, and high deuteration levels (N2D+/N2H+~0.5), suggestive of an evolved, prestellar stage.
  Aims. Corona Australis 151 appears to be an evolved prestellar core, but the presence of broad wings in some of the detected lines and a tentative 70micron detection with Herschel partially challenges its prestellar stage. We intend to assess its evolutionary stage.
  Methods. We analyse new ALMA data of the continuum emission and of several line tracers (including typical outflow tracers) at a resolution of~150-200au, tracing the envelope.
  Results. We unveil the presence of a compact and young outflow (projected dynamical age:~500yr), traced by SiO, CO, and H2CO emission. The continuum emission traces an envelope structure of size~1000 au and mass 0.33M_sun(assuming Tdust=20 K).
  Conclusions. Corona Australis 151 is an extremely young protostar, possibly one of the youngest known in the Solar neighbourhood, and hence a new laboratory to study the chemical and dynamical evolution at the dawn of star formation.

AI.tldr: This paper uses new ALMA observations to characterize Corona Australis 151, previously identified as a candidate evolved prestellar core. The high-resolution data reveal a compact, young outflow (~500 yr dynamical age) traced by SiO, CO, and H2CO, plus a ~1000 au envelope of mass 0.33 Msun. These findings overturn its prestellar classification, showing CrA 151 is actually an extremely young protostar, one of the youngest known in the Solar neighbourhood.
AI.motivation: CrA 151 was initially identified as a promising evolved prestellar core candidate due to its centrally peaked structure, high densities, and deuteration, but ambiguous signatures (broad line wings, tentative 70um detection) challenged this interpretation. The authors aim to definitively assess its evolutionary stage using higher resolution observations.
AI.method: The authors analyze new ALMA observations at ~150-200 au resolution, including continuum emission and multiple molecular line tracers (SiO, CO, H2CO) sensitive to outflows and envelope structure, probing the collapsing material around CrA 151.
AI.result: ALMA data reveal a compact, young outflow with a projected dynamical age of ~500 yr, traced by SiO, CO, and H2CO emission. The dust continuum traces an envelope of ~1000 au in size with a mass of 0.33 Msun (assuming Tdust=20 K).
AI.conclusion: CrA 151 is not a prestellar core but rather an extremely young protostar—potentially among the youngest known in the Solar neighbourhood—making it a unique laboratory for studying chemical and dynamical evolution at the onset of star formation.

title: PPN--spin degeneracies in mock S62-like stellar-orbit inference
comment: 21 pages, 15 figures
summary: We investigate the degeneracies between black hole (BH) spin effects and parametrized post-Newtonian (PPN) parameters in the relativistic orbital dynamics of S2-like and S62-like stars orbiting Sagittarius A$^{\ast}$. Using a 1PN+SO Hamiltonian framework and synthetic astrometric and radial velocity datasets, we perform Bayesian parameter inference. For current baseline observational precisions, the dominant relativistic observable--the Schwarzschild periapsis advance--allows the recovery of the effective precession parameter $Υ$, while leaving the individual PPN parameters $γ$ and $β$ degenerate. Assuming microarcsecond-level astrometric precision, the spin-induced Lense-Thirring signal becomes partially detectable; fixing the PPN sector to General Relativity allows the BH spin magnitude to be constrained to an uncertainty of $\sim10^{-2}$. However, simultaneously varying PPN and spin parameters reveals a strong, approximately linear covariance between $Υ$ and the dimensionless spin parameter $χ$. To overcome this limitation, we demonstrate that joint multi-star inference can disentangle the degeneracy by combining a wider-orbit star, which constrains the dominant 1PN sector, with a compact relativistic orbit that is sensitive to Lense-Thirring frame dragging.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the degeneracy between black hole spin effects and parametrized post-Newtonian (PPN) parameters in the orbital dynamics of stars (S2-like and S62-like) orbiting Sagittarius A*. Using a 1PN+SO Hamiltonian framework and Bayesian inference, the authors find that current observations can recover the effective precession parameter Υ but leave individual PPN parameters degenerate. While microarcsecond-level astrometry enables partial detection of the Lense-Thirring signal and spin constraints to ~10^-2 (when PPN is fixed to GR), simultaneously varying PPN and spin parameters reveals a strong linear covariance between Υ and the dimensionless spin χ. Joint multi-star inference—combining a wide-orbit star (constraining the 1PN sector) with a compact relativistic orbit (sensitive to frame dragging)—is shown to disentangle this degeneracy.
AI.motivation: The study aims to understand and overcome the degeneracies that arise when jointly constraining post-Newtonian gravity parameters and black hole spin from stellar orbits around Sagittarius A*, particularly as observational precision improves toward microarcsecond-level astrometry. This is crucial for correctly interpreting tests of General Relativity in the Galactic Center.
AI.method: The authors employ a 1PN+SO (first-order post-Newtonian plus spin-orbit) Hamiltonian framework to model stellar orbits. They generate synthetic astrometric and radial velocity datasets for S2-like and S62-like stars and perform Bayesian parameter inference to explore the parameter covariance structure between PPN parameters (γ, β, Υ) and the BH spin magnitude. They also test a joint multi-star inference strategy combining wide and compact orbits.
AI.result: Current baseline precision recovers Υ but leaves γ and β individually degenerate. At microarcsecond astrometric precision, the Lense-Thirring signal is partially detectable; fixing PPN to GR constrains spin to ~10^-2 uncertainty. However, jointly varying PPN and spin yields a strong approximately linear covariance between Υ and χ. Joint multi-star inference successfully disentangles this degeneracy.
AI.conclusion: The dominant relativistic precession observable alone cannot separate PPN gravity parameters from black hole spin effects. Combining orbits of different scales—a wide-orbit star probing the 1PN sector and a compact relativistic orbit sensitive to frame dragging—enables the degeneracy to be broken, allowing cleaner simultaneous constraints on both fundamental gravity parameters and the central black hole's spin.

title: The dispersal law of young star clusters: free expansion -- A Gaia/eROSITA census of Orion and Sco--Cen
comment: Submitted to A&A. Comments are welcome
summary: We measure how young star clusters disperse over time in the two nearest star-forming complexes. Our sample comprises 44 \texttt{SigMA}-\textit{Gaia}-defined clusters in Orion and 31 in Sco--Cen, with isochronal ages of 2--25\,Myr. We extend each cluster's census with \textit{eROSITA}-selected young stars that share its parallax and motion and lie within the distance they could have traveled ballistically since birth. By 10--30\,Myr, about one in three former cluster stars lies outside the cluster's cataloged boundary. Across both complexes and the full age range, we find that (1) the half-member radius increases linearly with age, $\rfifty \simeq \sigbirth t$, (2) the velocity dispersion shows no measurable evolution, and (3) all studied clusters are unbound. These results support free expansion. Young clusters in Orion and Sco-Cen emerge unbound from their birth clouds and coast at their birth velocity dispersion without significant relaxation or a characteristic dispersal timescale. We further show that memberships defined by density contrast preferentially omit the fastest stars, making the same clusters appear to expand more slowly ($\propto t^{0.6}$), cool with age, and approach equilibrium.

AI.tldr: This paper measures the dispersal of 44 young star clusters in Orion and 31 in Sco-Cen (ages 2-25 Myr) using Gaia and eROSITA data. The authors find that clusters emerge unbound from their birth clouds, expand freely with half-member radius increasing linearly with age, show no velocity dispersion evolution, and have no characteristic dispersal timescale. They demonstrate that density-contrast-based membership definitions bias results by omitting the fastest stars, making clusters appear to expand more slowly and approach equilibrium.
AI.motivation: To understand how young star clusters disperse over time in the two nearest star-forming complexes, and to determine whether the observed expansion properties reflect true physical processes or are artifacts of membership selection methods.
AI.method: The study utilizes 44 SigMA-Gaia-defined clusters in Orion and 31 in Sco-Cen with isochronal ages of 2-25 Myr. The cluster census is extended using eROSITA-selected young stars that share parallax and motion and lie within ballistic travel distance since birth. Cluster properties analyzed include half-member radius evolution, velocity dispersion, and binding state. A comparison is made between density-contrast-defined memberships and extended memberships.
AI.result: By 10-30 Myr, about one in three former cluster stars lies outside the cataloged cluster boundary. Half-member radius increases linearly with age (r ∼ σ_birth t), velocity dispersion is non-evolving, and all studied clusters are unbound, supporting free expansion. Memberships defined by density contrast preferentially omit the fastest stars, making clusters appear to expand more slowly (∝ t^0.6), cool with age, and approach equilibrium—a biased result.
AI.conclusion: Young clusters in Orion and Sco-Cen emerge unbound from their birth clouds, expand freely at their birth velocity dispersion, and lack both significant relaxation and a characteristic dispersal timescale. Previous apparent evidence of slowing expansion and thermal evolution is an artifact of density-based membership selection biases that exclude fast-moving stars.

title: Stellar Population and Dynamical Modeling of Galaxies with Kinematically Misaligned Components: Age and Metallicity of Structural Components
comment: 31 pages, 16 figures, 4 tables
summary: We present stellar population and orbit modeling of two galaxies with kinematically misaligned components, PGC 35706 and LEDA 2220522, extending previous Schwarzschild dynamical models. Using spatially resolved age and metallicity maps from NBursts full spectral fitting of MaNGA data with the E-MILES grid, we solve a regularized bounded linear inverse problem that assigns light-weighted SSP-equivalent age, metallicity, and mass-to-light ratio to orbital cells in the $(R,λ_z)$ plane. Component means and radial profiles use projected mass within the actual MaNGA field of view; profile segments with local component fractions below $1\%$ are treated as weakly constrained. In LEDA 2220522, the counter-rotating disk is younger than the co-rotating disk, $1.32\pm0.04$ versus $1.61\pm0.06$ Gyr, and more metal-rich, $[\mathrm{M/H}]=-0.450\pm0.043$ versus $-0.613\pm0.024$. Its rotation agrees with that of the H$α$ ionized gas, supporting late supply of chemically enriched retrograde gas without requiring multiple accretion episodes with alternating angular momentum. In PGC 35706, the counter-rotating disk contains $8.8\%$ of the mass in the observed field and is formally older than the co-rotating disk by $1.36\pm0.51$ Gyr and more metal-poor by $0.130\pm0.046$ dex. These differences are preliminary because the projected data provide limited support. Fifty Monte Carlo realizations confirm stability of the projected maps against statistical noise, but not uniqueness in individual phase-space cells. The stellar population and orbit approach is therefore applicable to MaNGA data when local projected component fractions and systematics from regularization and the dynamical model are explicitly considered.

They find that in LEDA 2220522 the counter-rotating disk is younger and more metal-rich than the co-rotating disk, while in PGC 35706 the counter-rotating disk is formally older and more metal-poor, though these differences are preliminary due to limited data support.
AI.motivation: To characterize the stellar populations and kinematics of kinematically misaligned (counter-rotating) components in galaxies, and thereby constrain the formation mechanisms—whether via late accretion of gas with reversed angular momentum or via multiple accretion episodes with alternating angular momentum.
AI.method: The authors extend Schwarzschild dynamical models with stellar population information. They perform NBursts full spectral fitting of MaNGA data using the E-MILES stellar population grid to produce spatially resolved age and metallicity maps. They then solve a regularized bounded linear inverse problem that maps light-weighted SSP-equivalent age, metallicity, and mass-to-light ratio onto orbital cells in the (R, λz) plane. Component means and radial profiles use projected mass within the MaNGA field of view, with segments below 1% local component fraction treated as weakly constrained. Stability was tested via fifty Monte Carlo realizations.
AI.result: In LEDA 2220522, the counter-rotating disk is younger (1.32±0.04 vs 1.61±0.06 Gyr) and more metal-rich ([M/H]=-0.450±0.043 vs -0.613±0.024) than the co-rotating disk, and its rotation agrees with that of Hα ionized gas, supporting late supply of chemically enriched retrograde gas. In PGC 35706, the counter-rotating disk contains 8.8% of mass and is formally older (by 1.36±0.51 Gyr) and more metal-poor (by 0.130±0.046 dex), though these are preliminary. Monte Carlo realizations confirm stability of projected maps against statistical noise but not uniqueness in individual phase-space cells.
AI.conclusion: The stellar population and orbit approach is applicable to MaNGA data for studying kinematically misaligned components, provided that local projected component fractions and systematics from regularization and the dynamical model are explicitly accounted for. The results for LEDA 2220522 favor late gas accretion without needing multiple accretion episodes, while the PGC 35706 results remain uncertain.

title: Rapid quenching and early gas depletion in the core of a galaxy protocluster at z=2.2
comment: 16 pages (of which 2 pages for Appendices), 9 Figures, 4 Tables. A&A in press
summary: Understanding how galaxy evolution is affected in forming high-z overdensities is a major open question in modern astrophysics. Here, we present the average properties of the quiescent galaxy population recently identified in the core of the Spiderweb protocluster at z = 2.16. By stacking observations from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST; F160W imaging and G141 grism spectroscopy), the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST; PaBeta narrowband imaging), and the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA; 1.2 mm dust continuum imaging), we constrained their ensemble star formation history (SFH), residual dust-obscured star formation, and cold gas mass, respectively. The inferred average SFH indicates steady stellar mass growth, with progenitor SFRs consistent with those of massive Halpha emitters (HAEs) in the same structure. This is followed by rapid quenching, on average 500 Myr prior to observation. No significant age differences are found between active galactic nucleus (AGN) hosts and non-AGN systems. We find weak PaBeta emission for 80% of the sample, yet with dust-obscured star formation rates consistent with quiescence in all but one source (ID 443) excluded from the sample. Our galaxies remain individually and globally undetected in the dust continuum, yielding an average gas fraction fgas= Mmol/Mstar<7%, consistent with previously reported gas depletion trends with stellar mass observed in neighboring HAEs. We thus find the Spiderweb protocluster to host a sizable population of gas-depleted, massive quenched galaxies in its core, likely descending from main-sequence galaxy progenitors and building the first elements of the red sequence in this high-z forming cluster.

AI.tldr: The study stacks multi-wavelength observations (HST, JWST, ALMA) of quiescent galaxies in the Spiderweb protocluster at z=2.16, revealing their average star formation history, residual dust-obscured star formation, and cold gas content. The quiescent galaxies grew steadily from main-sequence-like progenitors, quenched ~500 Myr before observation, and are gas-depleted (fgas<7%), constituting early red-sequence elements in this high-z forming cluster.
AI.motivation: Understanding how galaxy evolution, specifically the build-up of the red sequence, proceeds in high-redshift overdensities like forming protoclusters remains an open major question in astrophysics.
AI.method: Stacked HST F160W imaging and G141 grism spectroscopy, JWST PaBeta narrowband imaging, and ALMA 1.2 mm dust continuum imaging to constrain ensemble star formation history (SFH), residual dust-obscured star formation, and cold gas mass of quiescent galaxies in the Spiderweb protocluster core.
AI.result: Steady stellar mass growth from progenitors consistent with massive Halpha emitters (HAEs); rapid quenching ~500 Myr before observation; no age difference between AGN hosts and non-AGN; weak PaBeta emission in 80% of sample but consistent with quiescence (except ID 443); individually and globally undetected in dust continuum, fgas<7%; gas depletion correlates with stellar mass.
AI.conclusion: The Spiderweb protocluster core hosts a sizable population of gas-depleted, massive quenched galaxies likely descending from main-sequence galaxy progenitors, building the first elements of the red sequence in this high-z forming cluster.
